chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abdullah ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, glorifies Himself three times every day and night. So whoever glorifies Allah with what He glorified Himself with, then if he was in a state of misery, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will turn him to happiness.
He should say: You are Allah, there is no god except You, Lord of the worlds.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Exalted, the Great.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, Master of the Day of Judgment.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forgiving, the Merciful.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Wise.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, from You the creation began and to You it returns.
You are Allah, Who, there is no god except You, You have not ceased and will not cease.
You are Allah, Who, there is no god except You, the Creator of good and evil.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Creator of Paradise and the Fire.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, One, Eternal, He neither begets nor is begotten, nor is there any equivalent to Him.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Believer, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Exalted.

Glory be to Allah from what they associate. He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Designer. For Him are the Good Names. There glorifies to Him whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Great, and the Greatness is Your Robe.

key_terms.الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ: The Creator, the Originator, the Designer

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication to recite to turn misery into happiness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific litany of divine attributes for daily glorification, linking spiritual remembrance to the transformation of worldly misfortune into happiness. The text explicitly connects these supplications to the Quranic concept of Allah glorifying Himself, citing verses such as Surah Al-Hashr and Surah Al-Ikhlas to establish the theological basis for these names. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* (monotheism) and the efficacy of aligning one's worship with the divine self-description found in the Quran.
